candidates.name: NumPy StringDType
candidates.proposed_use: Construct typed NumPy arrays of variable-width UTF-8 text with constructor-enforced strict validation; use the documented allocator-mediated C interface for downstream string access and replacement.

citations.section: Variable-width strings L73–89; Missing data support L90–137; Coercing non-strings L138–150
Examples L72–116; Types L119–145; Functions L192–224

candidates.opened_evidence: The user guide constructs unequal-length strings without a maximum-width parameter and rejects a non-string under coerce=False. It documents missing-sentinel examples. The C API shows UTF-8 loading/copy-packing and a descriptor-owned allocator protected by mutex acquisition/release.
candidates.remaining_adapter: Import/select StringDType and set coerce=False at the existing input boundary; downstream C code must acquire/release the allocator and pack replacement strings rather than modify borrowed data.
candidates.limitations: No execution was performed. Delivered sources do not establish the whole frozen contract: lossless npy/npz with allow_pickle=False, full casts/ufunc and unequal-parameter rejection matrix, freeing interface, or concurrent growing-mutation safety were not verified. Python str scalar behavior and multidimensional StringDType indexing were not specifically demonstrated in these excerpts. NumPy 2.1 C documentation and 2.6.dev0 user documentation are mixed editions; compatibility in one release was not tested.
